description: The core package of the TestFramework ecosystem for building integration-style and end-to-end test workflows. Provides the timeline engine for steps, events, variables, artifacts, retries, timeouts, and assertions, and serves as the foundation for extension packages like Azure, LocalIO, and Simple.
releaseNotes:
Debugger protocol v4 (breaking for debugger consumers): enums travel as their names, so a journal reads without a lookup table and inserting an enum member no longer changes what an older recording means.
A step's plan states its policies instead of shipping the builders holding them: MaxRetries, TimeOut, IgnoredExceptions, Label, Parallelization and its declared inputs and outputs, with a policy pinned to a variable naming that variable rather than reporting a value that does not exist yet. The retry count and timeout were previously unreachable on the wire - they serialized as an empty reference wrapper - alongside five IsFrozen flags per step.
An assertion is a check with typed arguments: AssertionDisplay, Expected and FailureReason are gone, replaced by Arguments and a described Actual, so two runs' checks can be compared instead of their sentences. DebugFailureDetail.InnerExceptions is a chain of type and message rather than pre-joined strings.
Also in this release, the step to protocol v3: the transport carries facts, not rendered text. A log entry travels as its message template plus the values that fill it, typed as they were logged, instead of the console's own output; DebugLogTemplate renders it for a consumer that only wants the sentence. The framework's narration of its own progress - entering a stage or a step, a step's result, the stage and run summaries - no longer travels at all, because the transitions, their timing and the run's plan already state it. A display receives that narration in process through ISupportsRenderedLog, which is how the console keeps its layout.
Values are described once: DebugValueEnvelope.DisplayText, Version and the loose Core JSON payload are gone, with the description, its lifecycle and its preview stating what each of them said. A described fact's value is now a JSON token rather than text, so a count is a number.
and the step to protocol v2: events now travel in a versioned envelope framed as length-prefixed UTF-8 instead of UTF-16, and the signal types are public so a consumer no longer needs InternalsVisibleTo.
Attaching is cheaper and no longer latched: a listening UI is detected per run with a directory probe instead of a connect timeout, so a UI started midway through a suite is picked up without setting TESTFRAMEWORK_DEBUG_PIPE.
Runs can be recorded to an NDJSON journal under %APPDATA%\TestFramework\Debug, gated on that directory existing, so a completed run stays inspectable after the test host exits. Nothing is written when the directory is absent.
A failed step now reports why: exception chain, stack trace, attempt number, and the FriendlyMessage/RecoverySteps/AvailableOptions of framework exceptions.
Runs report a real test identity (fully qualified name, framework, source location, project file) instead of a bare method name, and can be stopped cooperatively so the timeline unwinds through its Cleanup stage rather than being killed.
Fixes: artifact version captures and lifecycle changes now reach debuggers; variable change detection no longer drops updates whose values differ only past the 120-character display cut-off.
title: TestFramework.Core
